$comment: What the user can do after an official upstream refuses an input. The one-tap action comes from the failed message's own recorded rejection (signature match in rejection-signatures.v1.json, official connection, before any output, the medium was actually sent), never from the projection or the negative cache of a later state; one action per refused capabilityKey, generic over image / file / video; a param_rejected match offers resending without that parameter; no match shows the upstream error as is and offers no media action. Every match also records the negative cache entry. The kill-switch reason is per medium: three copy ids disabled.kill_switch.image / .file / .video, never one image-only string for all media. Card layout when a one-tap action is offered: exactly two buttons, the action first and switch_model second (expect.secondaryAction), switch_model always shown, no edit-message button. Cases without an action do not constrain the generic error card. Each end names its tests REJECTION_RECOVERY_<id> (Web: it('REJECTION-RECOVERY-<id> ...')).
